job.text: No, not soft, that is the very last adjective applicable to the Land's End. Even on that calm day there was a fresh wind--there must be always wind--and the air felt sharper and more salt than any sea-air I ever knew. Stimulating too, so that one's nerves were strung to the highest pitch of excitement. We felt able to do anything, without fear and without fatigue. So that when a guide came forward--a regular man-of-war's-man he looked--we at once resolved to adventure along the line of rocks, seaward, "out as far as anybody was accustomed to go." "
